chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions, raised the hadith, saying:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he intended to marry a woman, would send someone to look at her, and he would say to the sent one: 'Smell her neck; if her neck is good, her scent (habit) will be good. And look at her heels; if her heels are trim, her knees will be large.'
ai.seo_question: What physical signs did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) look for when evaluating a woman for marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the permissibility of pre-marital observation in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing physical attributes as indicators of overall health and character. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) instructed the envoy to assess the bride's neck and heels, linking external beauty to internal purity and robust constitution. This practice underscores the importance of mutual compatibility and careful selection in marital unions, a key theme in Shia family law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of our companions raising the Hadeeth,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> intended to marry a woman, sent over a woman to look at her and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying to the sent woman: ‘Smell her neck, for if her neck is good her customary habits would be good, and look at her heels, for if her heels are trim her knees would be large’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from certain persons of our people in a marfu’ manner has said the following: “

When the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, wanted to marry a woman he would send a woman to examine her with the instruction, ‘Smell her neck; if it smells fine her scent smells fine, and if her soles are full, her knees are large.’”
